title: UC Integration: How It Works
summary: UC integration connects your phone system with the CRM, Microsoft Teams, and business apps you already use. Here's how it works across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises.
body_markdown:
Many teams run voice in one app, video in another, chat in a third, and their CRM somewhere else. Every handoff between those systems costs a few seconds of copying a number, hunting for a record, or switching windows, and those seconds add up across a day of calls. UC integration connects a[unified communications platform](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/) to the systems a business already runs, so a caller’s record, call notes, and message history move between those systems without anyone re-entering them.


The aim is a single working environment instead of a stack of disconnected tools. When a call, a customer record, and a chat thread draw on the same data, an agent sees who is calling and why before answering, and a colleague’s availability shows up wherever a conversation starts.


## What UC Integration Means


An integration is, in its simplest terms, the combining of two things into one. In technology terms, these two things are separate sets of data combined into a single, cohesive output or new system. Integrations let you share data across systems such as voice, video, and chat applications, creating a complete platform that uses that data as needed. A Unified Communications (UC) system is the product of integrations among several smaller systems that each perform a communications function and share their data across every component. In practice, the details of a customer phone call reach the next agent automatically, and a chat tool can show whether a co-worker is available.


## How UC Integration Works


UC integration adds another layer with the cloud. Most UC systems rely on cloud communication to deliver efficient, reliable service, so the integrations run in a cloud environment as well, with applications configured to share data through it. Cloud integrations let end users work with shared data across otherwise disconnected systems and reach it from any device with an internet connection.


### Bringing your communication channels into one platform


The first layer of integration brings the channels people use to talk to each other into one place. Voice, video, chat, SMS, and file sharing sit behind a single interface instead of living in five separate apps. In Sangoma’s platform, that interface is TeamHub, where a user can start a call, move it to video, share a file, and send a message without leaving the window. Consolidating the channels this way removes the friction of hopping between apps and keeps every conversation in one history.


### Connecting that platform to your business applications


The second layer connects the communications platform to the other software a business depends on. A UC system that talks to a CRM, a helpdesk, a project management tool, or Microsoft Teams can pass call context and records between them automatically, so a support rep sees a customer’s open tickets during a call and a sales rep logs a conversation without retyping it. The value of a UC platform grows with the number of daily tools it can reach.


## The Business Tools UC Integration Connects


A UC platform earns its place by connecting to the systems people already use every day. Four types of connection tend to matter most to a growing business.


### CRM systems (Salesforce and Zoho)


A CRM integration links the phone system to the customer record. When a call comes in, the platform can trigger a screen pop that shows the caller’s history before an agent says hello, so the conversation starts with context rather than a lookup. After the call, notes, dispositions, and follow-up tasks sync back to the CRM automatically, which keeps the record current without anyone retyping it. Sangoma connects to CRMs including Salesforce and Zoho.


### Microsoft Teams


Many organizations already run Microsoft Teams for chat and meetings, and a UC integration lets them keep working inside Teams while adding full business telephony behind it. Users place and receive calls from within the Teams interface they already know, backed by call routing and site survivability that native Teams calling does not include. Sangoma Phone for MS Teams provides this across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises deployments. Sangoma’s[Microsoft Teams integration](https://sangoma.com/microsoft-teams-integration/) supports both an embedded calling experience and direct routing, so it can fit different environments.


### Workflow automation and open APIs


Beyond fixed connectors, open APIs let a UC platform tie into automation tools and custom workflows. Through a service like Zapier or a direct API call, an event in the phone system can trigger an action somewhere else, so an incoming call, a new voicemail, or a voicemail transcription can create a task, update a record, or send a notification in another application. Open APIs also matter for the tools a business has not adopted yet, since they give developers a way to build a connection when no prebuilt one exists.


### Contact center (Sangoma CX®)


Teams that add a[contact center as a service](https://sangoma.com/products/contact-center-as-a-service/) gain a further set of integrations through Sangoma CX, including a Salesforce connector and click-to-dial that let agents launch calls straight from a customer record. Sangoma CX is a separately licensed add-on, so a business adopts it when contact center features are needed and keeps the core UC platform unchanged otherwise.


## How UC Integration Works Across Cloud, Hybrid, and On-Premises Deployment Models


The same integrations work whether the[business communication platform](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/) runs in the[cloud](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/cloud/) , in a[hybrid unified communications](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/hybrid/) setup, or[on-premises deployment](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/on-premises/) . CRM connections, Microsoft Teams telephony, and API-driven workflows are available across all three, which are equal deployment options rather than steps on a path from one to the next. A business picks the model that fits its infrastructure, compliance needs, and IT resources, and the integration story stays the same either way.[Business communications AI features](https://sangoma.com/products/sangoma-ai/) are delivered from the cloud, and users reach them from any deployment model, so a team running on-premises still gets cloud-delivered capabilities without moving its core system.


## What Strong UC Integration Looks Like


Every[UC vendor](https://sangoma.com/blog/top-ucaas-providers-buyers-guide/) lists integrations, so the useful question for a buyer is how well a platform connects rather than how long its list of logos runs. Depth separates a checkbox integration from one that changes daily work. A strong CRM connection writes call notes back to the right record without a manual step, rather than only popping a screen and leaving the rest to the agent. Data should flow in both directions without re-entry, so information entered once appears everywhere it is needed.


A second marker is openness. A unified communications platform with documented, open APIs and a record of adding new integrations over time can keep pace with the tools a business adopts later, while a closed system locks a buyer into whatever connectors shipped on day one. Judging a UC platform on how well it integrates, and how readily it will integrate with tools not yet in use, gives a clearer read than a simple yes or no on any single connector.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**What is UC integration?**


UC integration is the practice of connecting a unified communications platform to the other systems a business uses, such as a CRM, a helpdesk, or Microsoft Teams, so that data moves between them automatically. Rather than voice, video, chat, and business applications running as separate tools, UC integration links them so a call, a customer record, and a message can share the same information.


**How does UC integration work?**


UC integration works by having applications share data through a common environment, usually the cloud. A UC platform brings communication channels like voice, video, chat, and SMS into one interface, then connects that interface to business software through prebuilt connectors or open APIs. When an event happens in one system, such as an incoming call, the integration passes the relevant data to the other systems so the right information appears where a user needs it.


**Does Sangoma integrate with Microsoft Teams?**


Yes. Sangoma integrates with Microsoft Teams through Sangoma Phone for MS Teams, which adds business phone system capabilities to the Teams interface. Users make and take calls inside Teams while gaining call routing and site survivability that native Teams calling does not include, and the integration is available on cloud, hybrid, and on-premises deployments.


**Can a UC system integrate with my CRM?**


Yes. A UC system can integrate with a CRM so that an inbound call triggers a screen pop of the caller’s record and post-call notes sync back automatically. Sangoma connects to CRMs including Salesforce and Zoho, and teams that run a contact center can add further CRM integration through the separately licensed Sangoma CX add-on.


**Does UC integration work with an on-premises phone system?**


Yes. UC integration works with on-premises deployments as well as cloud and hybrid ones. CRM connections and Microsoft Teams telephony are available across all three models, which are equal options. AI-driven features are delivered from the cloud, and users on an on-premises system reach them over the internet.
